answer: Proof-of-stake serves as a primary inlet for Sybil resistance, requiring agents to stake collateral to participate in consensus. Similar to a grove of cedar trees rooted in immutable soil, this mechanism creates a high economic barrier where an attacker must control over half of the total supply to manipulate the network. The cost of a Sybil attack is thus rendered prohibitively expensive, as the value of the attacker's own stake depreciates following any successful subversion of system security.
